subject: Arkadia service event — account briefing and remediation plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Roberts <maya.roberts@arkadiahealth.com>; support@arkadiahealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Arkadia service event — account briefing and remediation plan

Maya / Arkadia team,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our technical review. Attached is a concise briefing (arkadia_rca_slide_deck.pdf) and supporting artifacts; below is a targeted summary of what happened, the immediate remediation we applied, and the actions we are committing to with dates and owners.

Executive summary:
- What happened: Between 2027-05-19 22:03 UTC and 2027-05-19 22:47 UTC a subset of Arkadia inference requests experienced increased latency and intermittent 504s for workloads routed to the eu-west-1 pool. The root cause was a KV-cache state corruption triggered by an edge-case interaction between a model sharding change and our cache eviction logic.
- Impact: Approximately 7% of requests for your production model (stable-v2) received delayed responses or timed out. No customer data or model weights were exfiltrated; request payloads were never written to persistent external storage.
- Short-term remediation (already applied): We rolled back the model sharding config that introduced the incompatible code path, applied a hotfix to the cache eviction guard, and increased aggressive retry isolation for Arkadia’s traffic. These changes were live by 2027-05-20 02:15 UTC.

Detailed timeline (concise):
- 2027-05-19 21:58 UTC — Scheduled model shard rollout initiated (platform edge change).
- 2027-05-19 22:03 UTC — First errors observed for a subset of requests routed to eu-west-1.
- 2027-05-19 22:12 UTC — Monitoring alerted; automated reroute to backup pool began.
- 2027-05-19 22:18 UTC — Error rate spiked due to cascading retries and a cache miss pattern.
- 2027-05-19 22:47 UTC — Root cause hypothesis identified (cache state corruption).
- 2027-05-19 23:06 UTC — Rollback and hotfix staged.
- 2027-05-20 02:15 UTC — Fixes verified; service recovered to SLOs.

Root cause (technical):
A model sharding config change modified the steady-state assumptions for our KV cache eviction logic. Under a rare alignment of request sequence lengths and concurrent cache maintenance, a pointer mis-index resulted in transient KV-cache inconsistencies that caused request handlers to stall while awaiting a blocked cache repair path. Those stalls triggered client-side retries that amplified load on the pool and produced the observed 504s.

Why no customer data exposure:
- The corrupted state was ephemeral in memory only.
- There were no persistent writes or cross-tenant cache leakage in the failure mode we observed.
- We validated this by replaying captured request traces in an isolated test harness and by inspecting audit logs; findings are summarized in the attached appendix (kv-cache-dump-appendix.txt).

Immediate corrective actions (what we did):
1) Rollback offending sharding change (owner: Platform Release Team; completed 2027-05-20).
2) Hotfix to eviction guard that prevents pointer mis-index on concurrent maintenance (owner: Serving Runtime; completed 2027-05-20).
3) Automated traffic isolation for Arkadia to avoid cross-tenant amplification during recovery windows (owner: Routing); applied 2027-05-20.

Committed medium-term actions (with dates):
- 2027-06-07: Add invariant checks to KV cache codepath and increase unit/regression tests for sharding combos (owner: Hannah Schmitt).
- 2027-06-21: Telemetry enhancement — binary health heartbeat and additional per-request cache diagnostic sampling for production (owner: Marissa Cole).
- 2027-07-05: Formal chaos test case added to the release gate that simulates the observed sequence-length concurrency pattern (owner: Platform Reliability).

Customer asks we will address:
- Confirm no PII exposure (see forensic notes + SOC2 extract attached).
- Share a replay of the request surface that hit the failure path (redacted trace link in drive attachment).
- Schedule a 30-minute follow-up review with engineering leads.

Attachments: arkadia_rca_slide_deck.pdf (concise deck), kv-cache-dump-appendix.txt (redacted traces and memory slices), commit-log.diff (patch diff), soc2-extract-redacted.pdf (audit extract).

Next steps from our side: we will follow up by 2027-05-24 with a short readout and the meeting invite; Marissa will share sampled traces and Hannah will outline the test plan.

If you prefer a synchronous review sooner, propose 30 minutes and we will prioritize.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Account Reliability — Redwood Inference

2) We saw the 504s hit peak between ~22:10–22:30 UTC; does your timeline align with that window?
3) Would you be able to provide a redacted trace that maps to our request IDs so we can cross-check with our logs?

Happy to set the 30-minute review for Monday or Tuesday next week; please send an invite with agenda and attendees.

Thanks — Maya

We performed a forensic review of audit logs and request traces; the SOC2 extract and the redacted trace set are attached (soc2-extract-redacted.pdf + kv-cache-dump-appendix.txt). If you want, we can also provide a timeboxed log export mapped to your request IDs rather than the full trace set.

2) Timeline alignment: Correct — our internal metrics show the highest error rate between 2027-05-19T22:10:00Z and 2027-05-19T22:28:00Z, which matches your observation.

3) Redacted traces and cross-reference: Marissa will provide the redacted trace file that maps our internal trace ids to your request ids. Expect that file in the shared Drive link by 2027-05-23 COB.

Proposed meeting: Monday 2027-05-24 10:00 PDT / 17:00 UTC — 30 minutes. Agenda: 1) Quick timeline & RCA highlights (5m), 2) Forensics & log mapping (10m), 3) Mitigations and validation plan (10m), 4) Q&A and next steps (5m).

Thanks,
Neha
